pr_title: API/BUG: Make `to_json` `index=` arg consistent with `orient` arg
pr_body:
Updates `to_json` with less surprising behavior with the `index` arg:
- split and table allow index=True/False (as before)
- records and values only allow index=False
- index and columns only allow index=True
- raise for contradictions in the latter two and update messages
- add test



- [x] closes #25513, closes #37600

issue_context.title: BUG: DataFrame.to_json ignores index if it is repeated in the DataFrame.
issue_context.body:
- [x ] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.
Similar to https://github.com/pandas-dev/pandas/issues/25513
- [x ] I have confirmed this bug exists on the latest version of pandas.

- [ ] (optional) I have confirmed this bug exists on the master branch of pandas.


#### Code Sample, a copy-pastable example

import pandas as pd

df=pd.DataFrame({'column':[0,1,2,3,4], 'probe':[0,1,2,2,3]})
df.set_index('probe',inplace=True)
out = df.to_json(orient='table', index=True) 

assert 'primaryKey' in out
```

#### Problem description
DataFrame.to_json ignores index if it is repeated in the DataFrame.
Since pandas allows dataframes with repeated indexes, 
the function `to_json` should be able to write them.
If you want to limit this functionality, at least one warning should be implemented.

Note that 'to_pickle' works fine with repeated indexes, as expected.

#### Expected Output
Not Error in assert

comments: I am not sure if this is a bug perse, since a json should not have a duplicate keys and some formats don't allow it, see [here](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/21832701/does-json-syntax-allow-duplicate-keys-in-an-object). We could maybe warn the user here, or document it properly.

I agree, but it does not happen with to_pickle(), for example.  I didn't know how to catalog this issue.
Anyway, using to_json(orient='table') with a DataFrame with duplicated indexes does not imply a json with duplicated keys.

Notice that only 'primaryKey': [<name of column>] needs to be included in the resulting json.
Comparing it to `to_pickle` isn't a worthwhile endeavor as pickle is an entirely different format / protocol. As mentioned above, JSON should have unique keys, though it isn't explicitly forbidden.

> Comparing it to `to_pickle` isn't a worthwhile endeavor as pickle is an entirely different format / protocol. As mentioned above, JSON should have unique keys, though it isn't explicitly forbidden.

Don't mean to necro and maybe this is a separate issue, but the issue I'm having seems more general than the title here suggests. The index is ignored period:

```py
import pandas as pd
# %%
df = pd.DataFrame({"a": [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6], "b": [1, 2, 3.0, None, np.nan, pd.NA]}).set_index("a")
df.to_json(orient="records")
# '[{"b":1},{"b":2},{"b":3.0},{"b":null},{"b":null},{"b":null}]'
# %%
df = pd.DataFrame({"a": [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6], "b": [1, 2, 3.0, None, np.nan, pd.NA]}).set_index("a")
df.to_json(orient="records", index=True)
# '[{"b":1},{"b":2},{"b":3.0},{"b":null},{"b":null},{"b":null}]'
# %%
df = pd.DataFrame({"b": [1, 2, 3.0, None, np.nan, pd.NA]}, index=range(5, 11))
df.to_json(orient="records", index=True)
# '[{"b":1},{"b":2},{"b":3.0},{"b":null},{"b":null},{"b":null}]'
```

My workaround this is `df.reset_index()`, but that creates unnecessary work in an application I need to be performant.

EDIT: Looks like my comment is a duplicate of #25513.

EDIT 2: Found elsewhere, but `df.reset_index(inplace=True)` benchmarked faster on a few quick tests.

@dshemetov the `orient="records"` keyword argument only serializes the columns and values by definition, so the index argument is ignored. We would accept a PR to raise if both `orient="records"` and index are passed - would you be interested in contributing that? If not can you open a separate issue so the community can find and contribute? Thanks!
Sure, I'll need a little time to get to it.

@mroeschke Pretty sure that #52143 fixed a completely separate issue. It is still the case that the index is silently not written when the index is duplicated, and there really should be at least a warning, if not an error as it is in #52143. 
The OP's example code, `df.to_json(orient='table', index=True)`, will not raise an error in the case of #52143, (`orient='table'` isn't even mentioned)
